blocks.text: Feed Charge Pump PU-2101B — Mechanical Seal Leakage
Isolate PU-2101B, swap to spare PU-2101A, replace mechanical seal cartridge
Mechanical seal of Feed Charge Pump PU-2101B failed on 12-Mar-2026, causing seal leakage and an unplanned feed reduction to the ARP reactor section.
ARP produced resin grade PR-5502 (Reactor Rate ± 13.6 T/H). Field operator noted minor seal weep on PU-2101B during routine round.
Seal flush low-flow alarm annunciated; visible feed seal leak with low suction pressure. Pump auto-tripped on low discharge pressure.
Feed section reduced; charge to reactor curtailed pending seal repair. Rotating team mobilized.
Seal cartridge & shaft sleeve inspected — seal faces heat-checked / worn (dry-running signature).
New seal cartridge installed, pump commissioned, feed restored to ± 13.6 T/H.
Problem: Mechanical seal of Feed Charge Pump PU-2101B failed on 12-Mar-2026, causing seal leakage and an unplanned feed reduction to the ARP reactor section.

PU-2101B seal MTBF trended down from 26 to 9 months over the last 3 cycles. Seal-flush flow had been intermittently below the 6 L/min design minimum during feed swings, indicating recurring dry-run exposure.
Mechanical seal of PU-2101B leaked / failed
Reduced charge feed to ARP reactor section
Feed reduction due to PU-2101B mechanical seal leak
No unplanned feed reduction due to PU-2101B seal failure (seal MTBF ≥ 24 months)

Recurrence of this equipment failure mode:
     Before = 1 case   →   Target = 0 case
Operated at 13.1–13.7 T/H vs rated max 18 T/H — within limit.
Suction pressure dropped during feed swing; NPSH margin < 0.5 m (spec ≥ 1.0 m) — cavitation risk.
Seal-flush flow measured 3–4 L/min vs 6 L/min minimum — seal ran dry intermittently.
Cooling water to seal cooler inadequate
Seal cooler outlet temp normal (42 °C) — cooling adequate.
Seal in service 11 months, within 24-month design life.
NG = current condition not meeting standard (problem)   •   G = meets standard
No low-NPSH / flush-flow interlock in DCS
No automatic trip or alarm on loss of seal-flush flow.
Feed-swing SOP allows fast rate ramp
SOP permits > 2 T/H per minute ramp, driving suction transients.
PM covers seal only, not flush system
Seal-flush plan (Plan 11) not on the PM check-sheet.
Operators trained; no competency gap identified.

ROOT CAUSE:  Premature mechanical seal failure caused by intermittent dry-running: suction cavitation during feed swings reduced NPSH and seal-flush flow dropped below the 6 L/min minimum, with no interlock to protect the seal.
Prioritized root causes (high impact) are addressed first via Corrective & Pro-Active Actions →
Install seal-flush flow switch with DCS alarm on PU-2101B
Add low-NPSH / loss-of-flush trip interlock in DCS
Roll out flush-flow switch to PU-2101A spare
Apply interlock standard to all API-682 seal pumps in ARP
Revise feed-swing SOP to cap ramp at 1 T/H per minute
Add seal-flush system (Plan 11) to PU-2101B PM check-sheet
Stage commissioning with bypass timer & operator brief
Weekly seal-flush flow & seal-pot level check PU-2101B
Quarterly seal condition & shaft run-out inspection

New bearing installed, lube-oil system flushed, cooler tube plugged, train restarted to 55 T/H.

blocks.text: Cooling Water Pump PM-4405B (Motor Driven) — Motor Bearing Failure (Overheating)
Start standby CW pump PM-4405C, isolate PM-4405B, replace motor DE & NDE bearings
Cooling Water Pump PM-4405B motor tripped on 08-Jul-2026 due to drive-end bearing failure from grease degradation and an over-extended re-lubrication interval.
Cooling-water system running on PM-4405B; motor DE bearing temperature trending up (68 → 84 °C).
Motor bearing high-temperature alarm; motor tripped on winding/bearing over-temp.
Standby PM-4405C started; cooling-water supply maintained at reduced margin.
Motor DE bearing found seized; grease degraded/carbonized. NDE bearing marginal.
DE & NDE bearings replaced and re-greased; motor recommissioned.
Problem: Cooling Water Pump PM-4405B motor tripped on 08-Jul-2026 due to drive-end bearing failure from grease degradation and an over-extended re-lubrication interval.

PM-4405B motor bearing temperature baseline is 60–68 °C. Re-lubrication was performed on a fixed 12-month interval regardless of duty/ambient. Bearing temperature was not trended in CMMS, so degradation went unnoticed.
PM-4405B motor DE bearing failed / overheated
Loss of one cooling-water pump; reduced CW margin (standby covered)
CW pump motor trip due to bearing overheating
No motor bearing failure due to lubrication (bearing temp < 75 °C, risk-based re-greasing)

Recurrence of this equipment failure mode:
     Before = 1 case   →   Target = 0 case
DE bearing reached 84 °C vs 75 °C alarm — grease breakdown.
Running current 132 A vs 150 A rated — within limit.
Fan cowl clean; ambient ventilation adequate.
Bearing in service 2 years vs 5-year design — within life.
NG = current condition not meeting standard (problem)   •   G = meets standard
Fixed 12-month interval too long for duty & ambient — grease degraded.
Bearing temperature not trended in CMMS
No condition-based trigger; only alarm at failure point.
PM-4405B not on the monthly vibration route.
Rounds performed per schedule; local gauge read.

ROOT CAUSE:  Motor drive-end bearing failure caused by grease degradation from an over-extended, non-risk-based re-lubrication interval, undetected due to absence of bearing-temperature trending, resulting in bearing overheating and motor trip.

Add motor bearing temperature trending & alert to CMMS

Extend bearing-temp trending to utility motor fleet
Add PM-4405B/C to monthly vibration & thermography route
Verify motor cooling-fan & louvre condition each PM
Use metered re-greasing per bearing volume calc

blocks.text: Product Blower BL-5702 — High Vibration (Coupling Misalignment)
Stop BL-5702, re-align coupling, replace worn coupling element
Product Blower BL-5702 tripped on high vibration on 17-Jun-2026 due to coupling misalignment and a worn coupling element, halting the OPP powder-handling section.
OPP running normal; BL-5702 vibration trending up (4.2 → 8.5 mm/s) with 2X harmonic rising.
BL-5702 vibration reached alarm (11 mm/s); blower stopped to prevent damage — powder handling section halted.
Coupling element found worn/cracked; laser alignment showed 0.35 mm offset (spec < 0.05 mm).
Coupling element replaced, unit re-aligned to < 0.05 mm, blower restarted to 38 T/H.
Problem: Product Blower BL-5702 tripped on high vibration on 17-Jun-2026 due to coupling misalignment and a worn coupling element, halting the OPP powder-handling section.

BL-5702 vibration baseline is 3.5–4.5 mm/s. A rising trend with dominant 2X harmonic over 2 days indicated developing misalignment. Alignment was last verified 14 months prior; no soft-foot / alignment check in the routine PM.
BL-5702 high vibration from coupling misalignment
Blower stop due to high vibration (misalignment)
No blower stop due to misalignment (vibration < 7 mm/s, alignment < 0.05 mm)

Recurrence of this equipment failure mode:
     Before = 1 case   →   Target = 0 case
Vibration reached 11 mm/s vs 7 mm/s alarm — misalignment signature.
Offset 0.35 mm vs < 0.05 mm spec — angular/parallel misalignment.
Bearing envelope/shock-pulse normal — no bearing defect.
Soft-foot 0.12 mm found on one foot — contributed to misalignment.
1X component within balance grade — no unbalance.
NG = current condition not meeting standard (problem)   •   G = meets standard
Alignment check not in routine PM
PM did not include periodic laser alignment / soft-foot check.
Elastomer coupling element run beyond recommended 12-month life.
Monthly route missed the fast-rising 2-day trend.
Laser alignment tool & trained technicians available.

ROOT CAUSE:  High vibration from coupling misalignment aggravated by soft-foot and an over-aged elastomer coupling element, undetected because periodic alignment/soft-foot checks were absent from the PM and the vibration route interval was too long.

Add periodic laser alignment & soft-foot check to BL-5702 PM
Track coupling element life & replace at 12 months
Roll out alignment check to all Class-A blowers in OPP
Create coupling-element replacement register for OPP trains
Shorten BL-5702 vibration route to weekly
Use wireless vibration sensor for continuous trend
